newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc firm, Swiss dealers dismiss SNB talk.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc firm, Swiss dealers dismiss SNB talk.

text.p: The Swiss franc ended firm amidst talk which traders here dismissed that the Swiss National Bank was abandoning its relatively expansive monetary policy.
Traders said the SNB took money out of the money market on Tuesday, but the move, linked to borrowing for the Swiss government, was seen as technical.
"The SNB will not tighten policy anytime soon, as long as an economic recovery is not assured," Credit Suisse First Boston analysts wrote in a market newsletter on Tuesday.

Tomorrow/next money was steady Tuesday morning but prices of eurofranc futures have fallen sharply. "It seems there are problems with distribution, which is usual at the year-end, and then the money market operations of the SNB were completely misinterpretted," said Michael Bernegger at CSFB.
Money market traders familiar with the SNB's operations said that the SNB had taken money from banks this morning.

But the moves, they said, took place in a market which was left quite liquid at year-end, and were seen as a short-term operation for the government. "It is just ordinary money market borrowing in the name of the government," one trader said.
One London dealer said market participants had short positions in Swiss francs coming into the start of the year, and the latest talk may have led to short-covering.
He said U.S. funds also sold dollars for Swiss francs.

Traders said as well that rumours of a "2.5 billion franc rescue package" by the Swiss government had heightened belief the SNB may turn less expansive. But Swiss traders said the Swiss government already said in December it was considering a package of public investment projects, and there appeared to be nothing new in the latest talk. They also doubted that the SNB would suddenly change policy on such proposals.
Technically, some traders believed mark/Swiss was well-supported at 86.40/60 Swiss francs after its latest decline.
* The dollar closed at 1.3515/3525 Swiss francs compared with 1.3536/3542 at Monday's close, and 1.3547/3553 at Tuesday's open.
* The mark ended at 86.49/52 Swiss centimes compared with 86.57/59 centimes Monday and 86.82/85 at the open. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
